item.title: 9 dead in shooting in US Pennsylvania
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
9 dead in shooting in US Pennsylvania Share - WeChat
NEW YORK -- Nine people, including two children, were dead following a shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania, on Friday, US media reported on Saturday. Police were called to Perry Street on Friday evening after eyewitnesses reported seeing a man firing a gun before he entered a home. Two women were found dead in the street, and more victims were later found dead inside the home, said Erie News Now. Police said that the suspect was also found dead with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound. The City of Erie authorities said Saturday that all nine deaths occurred before police arrived at the scene. No additional gunshots were fired after police arrived. Police have not yet released the identities of those killed or discussed a possible motive.

item.title: Saudi-led coalition vows firm response to airport attack
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
Saudi-led coalition vows firm response after deadly attack on Riyadh airport RIYADH -- The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen has vowed to respond firmly to a Houthi attack on a passenger terminal at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday that killed 12 people and injured 309 others. Coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Malki said early Sunday on social media platform X that the coalition's Joint Forces Command would respond firmly to what he described as a "terrorist attack" in accordance with international humanitarian law. In separate posts on Sunday, Al-Malki said the Saudi-led coalition had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile and a drone launched by the Houthi group toward Saudi Arabia. The fatalities in the airport attack included four Saudi citizens and eight foreign residents -- two Bangladeshis and one each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan, according to the Saudi aviation authority. The authority said the injured were receiving treatment at several hospitals, with some in serious condition, and that airport operations had been temporarily suspended. The attack came as the Houthi group and Saudi Arabia continued exchanging strikes on major airports and other facilities. Three people were killed and 36 others injured in two separate attacks targeting Abha International Airport in southwestern Saudi Arabia and King Khalid International Airport on Tuesday and Wednesday, respectively. On Thursday, three Saudi citizens, including a pilot, were killed and several others of other nationalities were injured in two Houthi attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport. Houthi-run al-Masirah TV reported earlier on Saturday that Saudi Arabia launched a new wave of air and missile strikes across Houthi-held areas in Yemen, targeting Sanaa International Airport in the Houthi-held capital, areas near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait and several northern provinces. Also on Saturday, Yemen's government forces said that more than 1,150 Houthi fighters had been "neutralized" and over 180 military and logistical vehicles destroyed or damaged in over 1,900 strikes across multiple fronts in Yemen over the preceding 24 hours. The figures could not be independently verified. Yemen has been mired in conflict since late 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and much of the country's north. A Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 in support of the internationally recognized Yemeni government, now based in the southern port city of Aden. The renewed fighting marks a major escalation after a UN-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted major hostilities. US President Donald Trump said Saturday that the United States "may" join Saudi Arabia in striking the Houthi group. "We just found out about the recent attack. So we'll make a decision. We move very quickly," he told reporters on the South Lawn of the White House. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Sunday strongly condemned Saturday's Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. "Attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are a violation of international law. These attacks must cease immediately," he wrote on X.

item.title: Tim Cook makes first China visit since stepping down
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
Tim Cook makes first China visit since stepping down as Apple CEO Tim Cook appeared in Guangzhou, Guangdong province, on Saturday, marking his first trip to China since stepping down as Apple's chief executive and his first visit as executive chairman of the company's board of directors. His itinerary began with a visit to the set of a traditional Chinese Wing Chun film, where a crew was using iPhone 18 Pro smartphones to capture the ancient martial art. Coinciding with Cook's arrival, Apple disclosed that committed investment for its second China Clean Energy Fund has risen to $212 million. The fund has roughly doubled in size since Apple completed an initial $100 million anchor investment last year. The increase reflects commitments from additional Apple suppliers such as Sunwoda Electronic Co Ltd. The fund has completed preliminary investments supporting a 260-megawatt wind project in the Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region and a 50-megawatt wind project in Shandong province, both now under construction. Apple also announced that more than 95 percent of its direct manufacturing in China now runs on renewable energy, as part of its goal to achieve carbon neutrality across its entire carbon footprint by 2030. Cook's China trip is directly tied to the 2026 meeting of the Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management Advisory Board, scheduled for Oct 13–14 in Beijing. This year marks the board's 27th annual gathering, which Cook has chaired since October 2019. Ahead of the meeting, the school announced three new board members: Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of Nvidia; Lisa Su, chair and CEO of AMD; and Marc Pictet, senior managing partner of Switzerland's Pictet Group. The advisory board, established in October 2000, brings together senior leaders from multinational corporations and academic institutions to strengthen ties between the school and the global business community.

item.title: The Long March: An enduring inspiration
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
Retracing the Long March: From the birthplace of 25,000 Li to a new journey In August 1936, in response to Mao Zedong's call, Red Army soldiers put pen to paper to recount their firsthand experiences of the Long March (1934–36). Their accounts were compiled into a book titled 25,000 Li, which was completed in Yan'an in 1937. Ninety years after the victory of the Long March, China Daily reporter Yan An visits Yan'an, the cradle of the Chinese revolution and the place where the book was completed, to explore how the Long March has become a source of inspiration for generations to come. The Long March: An Enduring Inspiration, a mini-documentary that pays tribute to the enduring spirit of the Long March, premieres online on Oct 12. Follow Yan An as she retraces the footsteps of the Red Army and explores what the Long March spirit means for those embarking on their own new journeys today.

item.title: Jingdezhen hails strategic guidance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Jingdezhen hails strategic guidance President's sustained attention steered porcelain capital's heritage list bid At a museum on the outskirts of Jingdezhen in Jiangxi province, children from nearby villages and visitors from across the country alike stand mesmerized as they witness the wonders of porcelain clay and ceramics in a spacious, brightly lit exhibition hall. Not too far away, unbroken stretches of lush forests thrive, hiding within them well-preserved ancient porcelain-stone mining sites. "The new museums and well-protected ancient sites are all the result of our efforts over the last few years while applying for World Heritage status," said Zhan Xinghua, deputy director of the Jingdezhen Municipal Culture, Radio, Television and Tourism Bureau. Zhan spent more than a decade working on the city's bid for a World Heritage listing. In July, the city, known as China's porcelain capital, succeeded in getting the Jingdezhen Handicraft Porcelain Industry Sites inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List. Zhan said the successful application for World Heritage listing could not have been achieved without President Xi Jinping's sustained attention to the city's ceramic culture. On Oct 11, 2023, Xi visited museums and ancient kiln sites in Jingdezhen. During the visit he emphasized on further growing and strengthening the ceramics sector to burnish the brilliant reputation of this "millennia-old porcelain capital" to an even greater luster. For Zhan, this was not an ordinary expectation. "It was Xi's sustained care and planning that allowed Jingdezhen to build up strength and succeed in making it to the World Heritage List, thereby filling the gap of a porcelain theme on the World Heritage list," he said. The decade-long bid process resulted in deep and comprehensive changes. Today, 196 ancient kiln sites are well protected, 108 historic alleys retain their original appearance, and 1,000-year-old porcelain-making skills continue to be passed down in an orderly manner. "From heritage protection to strategic empowerment, the president mapped out a clear growth path for Jingdezhen's World Heritage bid," said Zhan. In 2015, three experts wrote reports about the difficulties that lay in the path of protecting a large number of porcelain shards unearthed at the Imperial Kiln site in Jingdezhen. Within one year, Xi made two important instructions on protecting the site. He required that "we must protect, study and make good use of the Imperial Kiln ruins, this treasure of Chinese civilization". The principle of "rescue first" was then adopted. "While we were already protecting ancient kiln sites and historic neighborhoods, Xi's instructions formally launched a path of inheritance and protection aimed at World Heritage status," Zhan said. In July 2016, Xi commented on a proposal by cultural and museum experts on Liangzhu's World Heritage application. He said: "World Heritage applications should help highlight the historical and cultural value of Chinese civilization, embody the spiritual pursuits of the Chinese nation, and present to the world a full and authentic picture of ancient and modern China." These three principles became the overarching guide for China's cultural heritage applications and directly guided the entire process of Jingdezhen's bid. In a 2019 trip to Jiangxi, Xi proposed building a Jingdezhen National Ceramic Culture Inheritance and Innovation Pilot Zone and creating a new platform for international cultural exchanges. This upgraded Jingdezhen's bid from basic relic protection to a systematic project integrating heritage inheritance, industrial upgrading, talent gathering and international exchange. In Zhan's view, from the 2015 instruction on protecting the Imperial Kiln site to the 2023 field visit, the top-level guidance has been consistent and progressive, providing confidence for the city's World Heritage bid. Living inheritance of cultural heritage forms the core foundation of the successful bid, something Xi has also repeatedly stressed. In 2023, Xi visited the Taoyangli historical and cultural district in Jingdezhen and explored ancient kiln sites. While talking with inheritors of the intangible cultural heritage of porcelain making, he said that "the fine traditional culture passed down by our ancestors must remain firmly in our hands. We should keep pace with the times and carry it forward". Yu Yin, 36, comes from a porcelain-making family; his father and grandfather both worked in the trade. He watched Xi's inspection tour on television and was deeply impressed. Now, to attract more young people to the craft, he is trying to combine ceramics with popular culture. "In Jingdezhen, porcelain inheritance has never been the persistence of a few; it is the passion and pursuit of a whole group of people," he said. Unlike some other traditional intangible cultural heritage projects that face a decline in the number of practitioners and a lack of successors, Jingdezhen attracts young artists and craftspeople from across China and the world, who settle in the city and devote themselves to traditional skills and ceramic innovation. The city is now home to more than 3,400 inheritors of intangible cultural heritage, over 100,000 young creative entrepreneurs, and more than 6,000 "foreign Jingdezhen drifters" from other nations, who have come drawn by the city's reputation. Xie Dongxi, 35, who holds a PhD in ceramic design, came to the city as a university student and has since rooted herself there, researching and creating ceramic art. In her eyes, the World Heritage inscription is not an end point but a new starting point for Jingdezhen. "The World Heritage status has put a thousand-year-old ceramic culture on the world stage. It has not only raised the city's popularity but also built a golden bridge for ceramic cultural exchange and mutual learning between China and the world," Xie said. Xie is currently collaborating with an artist from Ghana on a co-creation that blends traditional Chinese ceramic aesthetics and porcelain-making techniques with overseas artistic concepts, allowing them to integrate and flourish together, thereby promoting ceramic culture beyond China and on the world stage. dengzhangyu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: No Chinese casualties reported in Panama quake
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
No Chinese casualties reported after Panama earthquake No casualties involving Chinese nationals had been reported as of Saturday night following a powerful earthquake in Panama, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said. The spokesperson was responding to media reports that a powerful earthquake and a series of strong aftershocks struck Panama on Friday, damaging buildings and roads and prompting evacuations across the country. "China expresses sympathies to the Panamanian government and people in the affected region. As of now, there have been no reports of casualties involving Chinese nationals in the earthquake," the spokesperson said in remarks published on the ministry's website. The Foreign Ministry and the Chinese Embassy in Panama will continue to closely monitor the situation and provide necessary assistance to Chinese nationals in need, the spokesperson said. The spokesperson also urged Chinese nationals in Panama to take precautions against secondary hazards caused by the earthquake.

item.title: Tibetan postman delivers Long March spirit across grasslands
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Tibetan postman delivers Long March spirit across grasslands Share - WeChat
On wind-scoured grasslands where Red Army troops trekked 90 years ago during the Long March, ethnic Tibetan postman Lhalung Dorje brings postal service to remote herding communities in Sichuan province. He covers the 3,500-meter-high "Long March mail route" in Zoige county, braving blizzards and boggy marshland through all seasons. Over 19 years on the job, he has logged nearly 580,000 kilometers and delivered more than 5 million pieces of mail without a single mistake, embodying the Long March spirit as a tireless messenger across the grasslands.

item.title: Xi on carrying forward Long March spirit
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
Xi on carrying forward Long March spirit Share - WeChat
This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, which lasted from 1934 to 1936. The arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. President Xi Jinping has always stressed the importance of carrying forward the spirit of the Long March, which has become a powerful spiritual force inspiring the Chinese people to overcome difficulties and advance from victory to victory.
